steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Jesus said "Where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them" (Matthew 18:20). Christians believe worship can be both corporate (together) and private (individual).

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: When comparing worship styles, remember that both have the same purpose (honouring God) but different methods. Catholic and Anglican Christians tend to prefer liturgical worship; Baptist, Methodist and Pentecostal Christians prefer non-liturgical or informal worship.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Forms of Worship
steps.body: 1. For Forms of Worship questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Forms of Worship to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two different forms of Christian worship. | "Liturgical worship is better than non-liturgical worship." Evaluate this statement.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 1) Liturgical worship follows a set structure with formal prayers, readings and sacraments. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
